modelAnswer: Natural science studies existing natural systems to understand how they work; its nature is descriptive.
For example, studying how species interact in a forest is natural science. Natural scientists follow the empirical cycle: observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, and conclusion.
Design science creates artifacts, such as tools, systems, or methods, to achieve specific goals; its nature is prescriptive.

For example, developing software to manage forest data is design science. Researchers follow the regulative cycle: problem investigation or identification, solution design, solution implementation, and solution evaluation.
Computer science studies how computers work, what they can do, and their limitations; it uses methods of both natural science and design science.
In the natural science of computer science, researchers study existing algorithms, such as QuickSort or MergeSort, to understand their efficiency and limitations.
In the design science of computer science, researchers create or improve tools and systems, such as a secure programming language or a more efficient database management system.
Therefore, natural science helps describe existing systems, design science creates systems to meet goals, and computer science uses both approaches to understand and improve computer systems.

explain.title: Science and systems
explain.body: Knowledge is our understanding of systems in the universe. Science is a systematic way to validate this understanding. Natural and design science both study systems, but they ask different questions and use different methods.

explain.title: Natural science describes
explain.body: Natural science is meant to uncover the objectivity and functionality of natural systems in the natural world. Its nature is descriptive: scientists seek to understand and describe natural phenomena. They follow the empirical cycle: observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, and conclusion.

explain.title: Design science creates
explain.body: Design Science is focused on designing and creating artifacts (tools, systems, methods) to achieve specific goals. Its nature is prescriptive: it aims to prescribe and create artificial systems. Researchers follow the regulative cycle: problem investigation or identification, solution design, solution implementation, and solution evaluation.

explain.title: Computer science uses both approaches
explain.body: Computer science is the study of how computers work, including at what they can do and their limitations. Its natural science approach studies existing algorithms and their characteristics. Its design science approach creates or improves tools and systems, such as software, programming languages, and database systems.

mistakes: Confusing the empirical cycle of natural science with the regulative cycle of design science.
Calling natural science prescriptive instead of descriptive.
Giving a design science example without stating the goal the artifact is meant to achieve.
Saying computer science uses only design science; the section says it uses methods of both natural science and design science.
Forgetting a supporting example when explaining a branch of science.
